jc.t: Golden kalash installation, diksha ceremony and 53rd birthday festival
w: One mile procession.

Swamishri consecrated the murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Ghanshyam Maharaj, Harikrishna Maharaj, Laxminarayan Dev, Hanumanji, Ganapatiji and marble murtis of Guru Parampara amidst Vedic rituals. The inauguration of the Shree Swaminarayan Mandir in Anand was a historic event because the devotees of Anand in the time of Shastriji Maharaj were the pillars of BAPS. The murti pratishtha assembly was at the Swaminarayan Nagar. ( see special report )

In the evening, from 7.00 pm to 8.30 pm the APC (Akshar Purushottam Chhatralaya) Ex-students Convention was held in the presence of Swamishri. Finally, the students honored the murti of Lord Harikrishna Maharaj.

Swamishri blessed 20 youths who had jogged with a torch from Limdi to Vidyanagar (148 kms) and youths who had cycled from Surendranagar to Vidyanagar (78 kms) on the occasion of Swamishri's 80th birthday celebration.

3 December 2000 dawned with the auspicious chanting of Vedic mantras at the newly built Swaminaryan Mandir in Anand. The murti pratishtha ceremony was performed by Swamishri amidst euphoria and divinity. The occasion was all the more significant because the town of Anand prides in playing a pivotal role in the development of the Akshar Purushottam Sanstha. Swamishri consecrated the murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Ghanshyam Maharaj, Laxminarayan Dev, Hanumanji, Ganapatiji and Guru Parampara. The 65 ft high, 104 ft long and 75 ft wide mandir will now breathe with 172 socio-spiritual activities of the BAPS.
After his morning puja, Swamishri performed pujan of bricks for the foundation of a Hari mandir in the village of Kalamsar.

This morning senior sadhus ritually installed the murtis sanctified by Swamishri at the newly built Swaminarayan Mandir in the village of Bharkunda. More than 5,000 devotees attended the pratishtha occasion.

Harikrishna Patel, a youth, had returned after a pilgrimage to Chhapaiya, the birthplace of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Harikrishna carrying his child Alok, said, "I had also taken him to Chhapaiya." Swamishri, touching the feet of Alok, said , "By having your darshan I have also done the pilgrimage." Swamishri respectfully touched the feet of a little child and showed his reverence for the birthplace of Shriji Maharaj and its pilgrims.

ds.t: A fine way to make life a mandir
w: A youth came for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. He earned a salary of barely four thousand rupees in the stock market. He said to Swamishri, "I too want to do financial seva for the mandir."
"He does not even have his own home yet, and his parents have also passed away," the sadhus said.
"Even so, I want to do seva," the youth said firmly.
Swamishri said, "It is fine that you do physical seva. This is not necessary."

"No, I want to do it. I have received by your grace and will receive more." While this conversation was going on, Swamishri realised that the youth smoked cigarettes. Swamishri immediately said, "First do one thing. Give up cigarettes, and whatever is saved from that, give as seva here."

Swamishri showed him a fine way to make his life a mandir. He turned his wasteful spending to the right path and gave it a constructive direction. When Swamishri has someone do seva, he firmly insists that the ideal values of an elevated life are also carved into that person.

Two satsangi brothers in Kolkata run a business taking furniture contracts. Many people work under them. A man who had worked for them for years suddenly passed away while working there. This man had no one before or after him. Whatever relatives he had were these people alone. He had kept his savings with them too. After his sudden death, the saved money remained with them. He had no relatives at all. Both brothers thought, "Why should we take anyone's earnings? Rather, if we give it to the mandir, it will be used for good work." And they offered the whole amount at the feet of Thakorji.

When this was told to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Swamishri said, "God's grace is upon you, so you think like this. Otherwise, who knew that his money was with you! Today, even when people know about someone else's money, they sit on it. But you have digested satsang in your soul."

In 1983, when Pramukh Swami Maharaj had a heart attack, the renowned cardiologist of Vadodara, Dr B. R. Patel, had treated Swamishri. Learning of Swamishri's health, he came specially from Vadodara today to ask about it. He asked Swamishri about his health. So Swamishri told him in detail what had happened. Finally, having heard about all the symptoms, Dr B. R. Patel said, "When there is something like this, we put our patients on complete rest for two or three weeks. There was no special physical exertion, nor was there any particular cold, yet this pain occurred, so it is good to have it checked." This was his opinion too.
Aruni Bhagat phoned from Sarangpur. He said, "Please take care of your health."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "In this world everyone's body falls ill. We are to live as God keeps us. Bhajan, devotion and seva are being done; that is what we have to do."
Aruni Bhagat said, "Since you are going to Mumbai, we will pray here to Harikrishna Maharaj that your health stays good."

Swamishri said, "It is the fruit of the prayers of all the sadhus and devotees in India and abroad that this body keeps going. Because all the sadhus, devotees, youths and women observe vows, austerities and malas, the body keeps well."

Aruni Bhagat said nothing more, so Swamishri said, "Look, God and the Sant are within our soul. Grieving does no good. Maharaj too fell ill. Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj all fell ill. Their divine play goes on for our happiness."

Today, on the third day of the yagna, after beginning the yagna, Mahant Swami Maharaj left the yagnashala. A line of cars moved in front of and behind his car. Thousands of devotees too were having darshan with folded hands, with devotion and full attention. But Swamishri appeared completely untouched by this honour and respect.

When the sadhus asked about this, Swamishri said, "(All this) is only because of Thakorji. When (my) jai is called, I consider it 'the honour of Thakorji and Akshar Purushottam Maharaj' and stay free! If Doctor Swami and others do dandvat, I pass it on to Thakorji...! Otherwise it would be a burden."
Having said this, after a short pause, he said, "Bhagatji Maharaj used to say, 'All these people are not following me, but Swaminarayan Bhagwan who resides in me...'"

Through these natural words, after clearly revealing his own true form, Swamishri at once took up the thread of servitude and said, "Not even a quarter percent of burden; everything is on Maharaj. We remain free."

Bhagwan Swaminarayan says, "The greatness of a Sant lies in his upasana and devotion to God. And secondly, the Sant's atmanishtha (realisation of the self) is the greatest greatness..." Today everyone saw this greatness in Swamishri.
Today, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was entering the dining room for his midday meal, a sadhu standing there said, "Please eat... eat whatever you like."
"We will eat love," Swamishri said at once. In these words of his echoed the line, "O friend! The Lord of the earth is hungry for love..."

After finishing his midday meal, Mahant Swami Maharaj was moving forward among the sadhus with folded hands to go to his bedroom. To enter by the main entrance here, one had to go around a little. So an idea came to the attendants and, pointing to the room's large window, they asked Swamishri, "Would you like to go in through this window?"

Swamishri at once said "Yes", and amid the delighted cries of the sadhus standing around, he entered the room through the window, laughing. So the sadhus and devotees waiting for Swamishri at the main entrance came running there. Seeing this, they too were filled with joy. One of the youths asked Swamishri, "Just as you entered this house by a shortcut, please show us a shortcut to Akshardham!"
"The Satpurush!" Answering in a single word, Swamishri went into the room.
The feeling "If one truly finds a Sant as helmsman, one reaches the other shore..." was steeped in his words.
Today, after breakfast, Mahant Swami Maharaj said to the attendant sadhu, "My food...!"
The attendant sadhu could not understand. Swamishri said again, "My food!"
Still not catching on, the attendant sadhu asked, "What, Swami!?"
Every day after breakfast the virtues of the sadhus are spoken of, and referring to this, with a slight air of "Don't you understand?", Swamishri said, "Imbibing virtues!"
Usually the virtues of others burn people's hearts, but in Swamishri's mind the virtues of others are his food.
